newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST- VNU SEEN UP 15 PCT, WEGENER 16 PCT IN 96.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST- VNU SEEN UP 15 PCT, WEGENER 16 PCT IN 96.

text.p: Publishers VNU and Wegener are expected to report rises in ordinary net earnings for 1996 of 15 and 16 percent respectively next week.
Both companies indicated early in January that their profits would rise by these percentages and analysts forecasts are therefore grouped in fairly tight ranges.
VNU, reporting on Tuesday, is expected to post an ordinary net profit of some 315 million guilders versus 274 mln in 1995.
Wegener, which publishes a day later, is seen posting a net profit of some 68.1 million guilders, up from 58.7 mln in 1995.
Unlike 1995 -- when the sale of a U.S. subsidiary brought in extraordinary income of 156 million guilders -- VNU is not expected to report any major extraordinary items.

Analysts said VNU's 1996 results should reflect another strong performance by its business information unit, buoyant advertising revenues for its regional newspapers and a fair performance from its consumer magazines.
Commercial television -- which has suffered from tough competition in the Netherlands and Belgium -- is expected to post a small loss after a 36 mln guilder profit in 1995.

Growth of Wegener's earnings per share is expected to lag overall profit growth -- rising some five percent -- due to the issue of new shares in part payment of last year's acquisition of compact disc (CD), radio and television group Arcade.

Wegener's regional newspapers and direct marketing business are expected to have driven earnings growth in 1996 but the Arcade CD and television operations both had a tough year due to slack consumer demand and the dogfight for TV market share.
Wegener has recently struck a deal under which U.S. group Saban will take a majority stake in Wegener's struggling Dutch television re-runs channel TV10.
Analysts expect the earnings of both VNU and Wegener to increase by some 15 percent again in 1997, pretty well in line with last year's earnings growth.
